prerequisites: Knowledge of the Python programming language

learning_outcomes.text: Upon successful completion of the course, students will understand the theoretical foundations and core algorithms of Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Retrieval (IR), and Machine Learning applied to textual data. In particular, they will understand the main approaches to language representation, lexical, syntactic, and semantic analysis techniques, probabilistic and neural language models, Transformer architectures, and Large Language Models (LLMs), as well as the methodologies used to evaluate the performance of NLP systems.

Students will be able to design and develop Natural Language Processing applications using dedicated software tools and libraries, implementing text processing pipelines, Information Retrieval systems, and text classification models. They will also be able to use pre-trained language models, design effective prompts, integrate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) techniques, and develop simple agent-based systems to address real-world problems.

Students will acquire the ability to critically evaluate different NLP techniques for specific application problems, selecting the most appropriate models, text representations, training methodologies, and evaluation strategies. They will also be able to interpret experimental results, identify the limitations and challenges of different models, and assess aspects such as robustness, explainability, and the overall quality of the developed solutions.

Students will be able to clearly and effectively communicate methodologies, algorithms, and results related to Natural Language Processing systems, using appropriate technical terminology in both written and oral form. They will also be able to present and justify their design decisions during the development of NLP applications and effectively discuss technical solutions with audiences possessing a computing background.

Given the rapid pace of innovation in the field, students will develop the skills required to independently deepen their knowledge of advanced Natural Language Processing techniques and tools by consulting scientific literature and technical documentation. They will also be able to adapt to ongoing advances in generative artificial intelligence, Large Language Models, and agentic AI systems, continuously updating their professional knowledge and skills throughout their careers

syllabus_topics: Lexical and syntactic analysis, part-of-speech tagging
Data structures for Vector space models
Machine learning improvement approaches. Feature selection. Rebalancing
Black box classification models: Support Vector Machines
Semantic analysis: Word Sense, Semantical Databases, relations between language terms
Advanced text representation models: word embedding
Development of command line interface agent-based systems
